title: Apply the grammar filter
summary: Use the words around a gap to work out what kind of word and what form it needs, before you look at the meaning.

sections.title: What kind of word goes here?
content: Read this: ‘The tired runners ___ across the line.’ Before you think of a word, ask what is missing. The sentence has a subject, ‘the tired runners’, but no verb. So the gap needs a verb, and the story is in the past.
This takes a few seconds and can remove half of a word bank.

sections.title: Ask three questions at each gap
content: What comes before the gap? After ‘the’, ‘a’ or ‘her’, expect a noun, or an adjective and then a noun. After ‘was’ or ‘felt’, expect an adjective. After ‘to’, a verb usually keeps its base form.
What comes after the gap? If a noun follows, the gap may be a verb or an adjective. If the sentence is already complete, the gap may be an adverb that adds how or when.
What form fits? Check past or present, one or many, and -ing or -ed. Words from the same family can look right but have the wrong form: ‘decide’, ‘decision’ and ‘decisive’.

sections.title: Cross out words that cannot fit
content: Take this sentence: ‘The ferry left ___ because of the storm.’ The sentence is complete without the gap, so it needs a word that tells us how or when. Suppose the bank has ‘late’, ‘lateness’ and ‘delay’. ‘Lateness’ and ‘delay’ are nouns and cannot follow ‘left’ here, so cross them out.
Now take: ‘Her ___ surprised the whole team.’ After ‘her’ the gap needs a noun, and it is the subject of ‘surprised’. If the bank has ‘decide’ and ‘decision’, only ‘decision’ fits.
The grammar check does not always leave one word. When two words still fit, read for meaning. That is the next lesson.

sections.title: Say the word class first
content: Before you choose, say what each gap needs: noun, verb, adjective or adverb. Then look at the word bank and cross out the words that cannot fit.

sections.title: Use the check on longer texts
content: Read each whole text first. Then use the three questions at each gap. These banks have words from the same family, so check the form as well as the word class.
Read your answers back in the sentence before you submit.

sections.title: Find where it went wrong
content: Word class error: I chose a noun where the gap needed a verb. Form error: I chose the right family but the wrong form, such as ‘decide’ for ‘decision’. Reading error: I looked only at the word before the gap and missed what came after it.
Meaning error: the word fits the grammar but not the story. Note this one for the next lesson.

sections.title: Try a new story
content: Complete one unseen story with eight gaps. You will see your feedback only after you answer every gap. If you need more practice, you will get a new story.
